case_name: Sri Dr Ravikumar S vs Smt Somya S O
facts_of_case: Appellant/husband and respondent/wife were married in 2010. They had a daughter born in 2012. The relationship was not cordial. Appellant filed a petition seeking dissolution of marriage on grounds of physical and mental cruelty, desertion, and incurable disease of unsound mind.

legal_principles.principle: Parties to a matrimonial dispute are required to describe the measure and standard of cruelty and lead cogent evidence to succeed in the plea of dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: However, parties to the dispute are required to describe the measure and standard of cruelty and lead cogent evidence to succeed in the plea of dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: The standard of proof in a case of matrimonial dispute pertaining to cruelty cannot be said to be applicable as is applicable in case of trial in the Code of Criminal Procedure.
legal_principles.held: However, parties to the dispute are required to describe the measure and standard of cruelty and lead cogent evidence to succeed in the plea of dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment dismissing the petition was upheld. The appeal was filed under Section 19(1) of the Family Courts Act, 1984.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
Section 13(1) (ia) and (ib) (iii) of Hindu Marriage Act
